name: Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v2-English-Hebrew-Codeswitching
notes:
ADDED 2026-10-25. A full finetune of nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 (run r6-en30), not a new base model: same FastConformer-TDT geometry, 600M parameters per the base card. Ship set is a single .nemo archive plus F16/Q4_K_M GGUF conversions; the .nemo is the model, the GGUFs are ports of it. Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base in a single table.

EVIDENCE CAVEAT, read before using this record. The repo is GATED: README.md returns 401 to an anonymous curl (https://huggingface.co/danielrosehill/.../raw/main/README.md -> 401; r.jina.ai mirror also 401). The numbers below were read from the rendered public model page HTML, which is served without auth and carries the full card. Base-column discipline holds there: the benchmark table has a column 'Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (stock)' beside 'v1.0 - Jachnun (this model)', on the same 84-clip clean subset, scored 2026-10-19, leaderboard round 3.

SCOPE CAVEAT, the one that matters. All training AND test audio is a SINGLE SPEAKER. The card says so outright: 'One speaker's voice: all training and test audio is the same speaker, so these numbers rank models on that speaker only. Gains on other voices are untested.' A 9.5% -> 3.3% WER drop on one speaker is speaker adaptation as much as it is language ability. Two held-out terms were also flagged by the author as possibly leaked into training. Confidence 0.6 rather than the usual 0.85 for that reason.

SECONDARY: the author's own held-out split (387 clips, Read-Aloud-Voice-Sentences rev 550bfcaa) is recorded as a row too, but it is the author's dataset, not a public benchmark, and the card itself calls the held-out gain 'within noise' while calling the seen-term gain real. That reading is correct and the rows are labelled accordingly. ENGLISH DID NOT REGRESS on the card's own numbers: own-English WER 1.7% vs stock 3.1%, LibriSpeech test-clean 1.2% vs 1.23% (card calls that within noise).

ARCHITECTURE FIELDS: inherited null from the base record and null for the same reason - a NeMo .nemo archive, no HF config.json, no safetensors metadata. Not zero, undefined-or-unverifiable. Params 0.6 is NVIDIA's card figure carried over, not a tensor count.

benchmarks.name: English-Hebrew code-switching WER (84-clip public benchmark)
benchmarks.config: Hebrish/English-Hebrew-Codeswitching-ASR-Benchmark test v1 clean subset, 84 clips, leaderboard round 3 (2026-10-19). Card table: this model 3.3% vs 'Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (stock)' 9.5%. Lower is better. All training and test audio is one speaker; other voices untested.

benchmarks.name: English-Hebrew term recall
benchmarks.config: Same public benchmark table, 84 clips / 172 term occurrences / 139 distinct terms. Card: 73.3% vs stock v2 32.6%.

benchmarks.name: Held-out dataset code-switching WER (387 clips)
benchmarks.config: Author's own held-out split of Read-Aloud-Voice-Sentences rev 550bfcaa, 387 code-switched clips. Card: this model 5.1% vs stock v2 11.3%. Held-out terms correct 47.8% vs 25.9%. Lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Held-out split, seen Hebrew test terms correct
benchmarks.config: Author's held-out split (Read-Aloud-Voice-Sentences rev 550bfcaa, 387 code-switched clips), 'Seen test terms correct' panel of the 'Same split, four models' figure: this model (v1.0, row 3) 72.7% vs stock v2 27.7%. Terms that were also in training; higher is better. Companion to the existing 47.8% unseen-term row - quoting only the 47.8% understates the gap the card is showing, quoting only 72.7% overstates transfer. Read off the card's chart figure by eye (vision read of hebrish.app/img/charts/*.png, 2026-11-01); figure values are printed labels, not axis estimates, so treat as ±0.1.

benchmarks.name: LibriSpeech test-clean WER (forgetting check)
benchmarks.config: Same figure, 'LibriSpeech test-clean WER' panel: other speakers, 200 utterances, this model 1.2% vs stock v2 1.2%. Unrounded per the figure's own footer: 1.20% vs 1.23%, which the card calls within noise - this row is a NO-REGRESSION check, not a win. Read off the card's chart figure by eye (vision read of hebrish.app/img/charts/*.png, 2026-11-01); figure values are printed labels, not axis estimates, so treat as ±0.1.

benchmarks.name: Own-English WER, same speaker (forgetting check)
benchmarks.config: hebrish.app 'English did not get worse' figure, 'Own English WER' panel: same speaker, 73 clips, this model 1.7% vs stock v2 3.1%. Not a public benchmark - author's own recordings, same speaker as training, so the gain is speaker adaptation as much as English ability. Read off the card's chart figure by eye (vision read of hebrish.app/img/charts/*.png, 2026-11-01); figure values are printed labels, not axis estimates, so treat as ±0.1.

benchmarks.name: Held-out split, unseen Hebrew test terms correct
benchmarks.config: Author's held-out split (Read-Aloud-Voice-Sentences rev 550bfcaa, 387 code-switched clips), 'Held-out terms correct' panel of the 'Same split, four models' figure: this model (v1.0) 47.8% vs stock v2 25.9%, Shakshuka PoC-2 44.4%, PoC-3 45.7%. Terms that were NEVER in training; higher is better. Companion to the 'seen test terms correct' 72.7% row: that one is the memorisation number, this is the transfer number. Read off the figure (hebrish.app/img/charts/*.png) by eye, 2026-11-01, full frame and a zoomed crop agreeing; printed labels not axis estimates, so treat as ±0.1.
